suggestions.title: Léon: The Professional
suggestions.description: Your list has Gary Oldman once, in The Dark Knight, and Natalie Portman not at all - this is the film that gave you both, in the same apartment corridor. Luc Besson wrote and directed his first English-language feature, shot in New York by Thierry Arbogast with a score by Eric Serra, produced by Patrice Ledoux for Gaumont and Les Films du Dauphin: $16 million in, $45.3 million out, released in France on 14 September 1994 and known simply as The Professional in the US before it was re-titled. Jean Reno is Leon, an Italian-American 'cleaner' whose entire life fits into one room, a pair of plant pots and a glass of milk, until twelve-year-old Mathilda (Portman, in her feature debut) comes home from a grocery run, walks past her own doorway, and keeps walking to his. Gary Oldman's Norman Stansfield, the corrupt DEA agent who did the shooting, is one of the great 1990s villains. Your action shelf - Heat, Die Hard, John Wick, Mad Max: Fury Road - is American and mostly kinetic; this is the European answer, an assassin film with almost no shooting in its first hour, built on two lonely people teaching each other to read and to shoot, and closing on a corridor ambush that everything since has been quoting. IMDb 8.5.

suggestions.title: Dr. Strangelove or: How I Learned to Stop Worrying and Love the Bomb
suggestions.description: You have had exactly one Stanley Kubrick in twenty-three batches, and it was the horror one. This is the other pole of his range: the end of the world as a comedy. Loosely based on Peter George's 1958 thriller Red Alert, which Kubrick and Terry Southern reworked after he concluded the material was far too absurd to play straight. Columbia financed and released it on 29 January 1964 for $1.8 million; it returned $9.7 million and runs 94 minutes, which is the fastest hour and a half in this entire database. Peter Sellers plays three roles - President Merkin Muffley, RAF exchange officer Lionel Mandrake, and the wheelchair-bound ex-Nazi scientist of the title - with George C. Scott as General Turgidson, Sterling Hayden as the paranoid General Ripper who starts the whole thing over fluoridation, and Slim Pickens riding the bomb down. Gilbert Taylor shot it, Anthony Harvey cut it, Laurie Johnson scored it, Tomi Ungerer drew the poster. Four Oscar nominations including Best Picture, Best Director and Best Actor for Sellers; seven BAFTA nominations and three wins, including Best Film From Any Source and Best British Film; and it was among the first 25 films placed on the National Film Registry in 1989. AFI ranked it 26th among American films in 1998 and third among its funniest. Your war viewing - Schindler's List, Saving Private Ryan, Apocalypse Now, Das Boot, Inglourious Basterds - has all been in the field, in the mud. This is the same century's war fought entirely from one war room, and it is still the funniest thing ever made about nuclear annihilation. IMDb 8.3.

suggestions.title: My Neighbor Totoro
suggestions.description: Two Studio Ghibli films have been through this portal already - Spirited Away and Grave of the Fireflies - and this is the missing half of the most famous double bill in animation history: Totoro and Grave of the Fireflies opened together in Japan on 16 April 1988, because Ghibli judged that neither film was commercially safe on its own. Written and directed by Hayao Miyazaki, produced by Toru Hara for Studio Ghibli and Tokuma Shoten, voiced by Noriko Hidaka, Chika Sakamoto and Hitoshi Takagi, scored by Joe Hisaishi, shot by Hisao Shirai, released by Toho, 86 minutes. A professor and his two daughters move into an old house in the countryside near the hospital where their mother is recovering from a long illness, and the film is quietly about the soot spirits in the walls, the camphor tree, the Catbus and a wood spirit only children can see. It took $41 million theatrically and far more on home video and merchandise, won the Animage Anime Grand Prix, the Mainichi Film Award and the Kinema Junpo Award for Best Film in 1988, and in Sight & Sound's 2012 critics' poll it was the highest-placed animated film of all time. Totoro then became Studio Ghibli's mascot - the reason the studio's logo is a giant grey creature. After the war films and the crime films, this is the gentlest 86 minutes anywhere on your list, and the one the dogs will happily sit through. IMDb 8.1.
